title: Calling `Image.resize()` on image from `CompressedTexture2D.get_image()` modifies the original image when called by EditorScript
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5.1, 4.4.1

### System information

Windows 11

### Issue description

I'm working on an EditorScript that creates thumbnails by cropping existing CompressedTexture2Ds loaded from disk.   

My code will:
1. create a copy of the image through `CompressedTexture2D.get_image()`
2.  resize the image with `Image.resize()`
3. save the image to a different location

Everything works as expected, until I run the script again. On following executions, the image size has been reduced to the results of the previous execution's resize. It's my understanding that `create_image` should create a copy of the texture's data, and manipulating the copied image should not modify the original texture in any way.

Running the following script multiple times produces the following output.

```
@tool
extends EditorScript
class_name ImageBug

func _run() -> void:
	var texture: CompressedTexture2D = preload('res://icon.svg')
	var image = texture.get_image()

	print(image.get_size())

	@warning_ignore('integer_division')
	image.resize(image.get_width() / 2, image.get_height() / 2)
```

output:
```
(128, 128)
(64, 64)
(32, 32)
(16, 16)
```

Interestingly, this is not an issue when this logic is embedded into one of my node's _ready functions, and I run the game normally. It's only a problem when I pulled it into an EditorScript. Also, the image size will reset when the godot editor is restarted.

A work around I've found is to create a new ImageTexture from the `CompressedTexture.get_image()`, then use the image from `ImageTexture.get_image()`

```
	# doesnt work
	var image = texture.get_image()

	# works
	var image_texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(texture.get_image())
	var image = image_texture.get_image()
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a new project
2. Paste the following code into a script, and run it multiple times

```
@tool
extends EditorScript
class_name ImageBug

func _run() -> void:
	var texture: CompressedTexture2D = preload('res://icon.svg')
	var image = texture.get_image()

	print(image.get_size())

	@warning_ignore('integer_division')
	image.resize(image.get_width() / 2, image.get_height() / 2)
```
